notebooks.title: Path Dependence and Preference Formation in Autonomous Systems
notebooks.summary: Revised analysis incorporating physical robotic implementations and reinforcement learning experiences to examine observable behavior stability.
notebooks.findings: Competent walking policies can be learned from physical robot experience, demonstrating robust adaptive behaviors directly from environment interaction. [source-ecc98936a06b4ec7]
notebooks.limitations: Physical robot experiments and simulation transfers provide domain-specific insights that require broader generalization across architectures.
notebooks.next_questions: How do physical embodiment constraints alter the stability of learned behavioral preferences compared to purely simulated environments?
notebooks.reason: Revising findings with newly collected evidence regarding physical reinforcement learning and semiotic interpretation.

notebooks.title: Theoretical Foundations of Artificial Agency and Moral Responsibility
notebooks.summary: Updated analysis integrating historical delegation frameworks and semiotic inquiry models into artificial moral agency requirements.
notebooks.findings: Ethical failures in artificial intelligence systems stem from human governance choices and delegation arrangements rather than autonomous machine malice. [source-4660da3bbcc74bfc]
notebooks.limitations: Historical and philosophical analogies require rigorous formal translation into computational agent architectures.
notebooks.next_questions: What computational mechanisms allow artificial agents to track and represent accountability structures internally?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating governance and delegation perspectives into artificial moral agency foundations.

notebooks.title: Epistemological Falsification and Bounded Rationality in Autonomous Agents
notebooks.summary: Revised examination integrating bounded rationality and automated planning into epistemological falsification frameworks for autonomous systems.
notebooks.findings: Bounded rationality provides a theoretical framework for decision-making and planning under resource limitations using information-theoretic ideas. [source-28b66dc2c66f4bd9]
notebooks.limitations: Findings integrate bounded rationality optimization principles and architectural planning models with philosophical epistemology.
notebooks.next_questions: How can real-time resource limits be dynamically budgeted during automated falsification loops?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook with new evidence on bounded rationality and automated planning frameworks.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
